# @arki/journal

> A journal for Drizzle entities. Every change is one immutable event row and one normal table row, written in one transaction. Projections run inside that transaction. Effects run after the commit, from a job table.

## Import paths
- `@arki/journal`: the core. `initJournal`, `need`, `jobId`, the command failures `CommandNotFound`, `CommandInvalid`, `CommandForbidden`, `CommandConflict`, `CommandError`, `isCommandError`, `JournalError`, `isJournalError` and the types, including `JobRunner` and `ScheduledJob` (the port that runs queue rows), and `combineRunners(...)` for a worker with several runners. Job operations live on the `journal` object (`jobs`, `job`, `jobCounts`, `retry`, `discard`, `cancel`, `retryDead`, `purgeDead`, `replayJob`, `archivedJobs`, `archiveStatus` and more). The retention policy types and `ndjsonArchiveSink` are exported too.
- `@arki/journal/pg`: `journalTables()`, the tables for the app's schema (`journal_events`, `journal_jobs`, `journal_job_attempts`, `journal_job_archive`, `journal_job_operations`, `journal_receipts`, `journal_cursors`).
- `@arki/journal/dot`: optional. The `@arki/dot` adapters `journal(...)` (driven, for `.use()`) and `journalWorker(...)` (driving, for `.serve()`, with an optional `jobs` source), and the feature slice `journalHandlers(...)`.
- `@arki/journal/orpc`: optional. The oRPC middleware `commandErrors()`, `actorRun(select)`, `idempotent({ scope })` and the function `toORPCError(error)`.
- `@arki/journal/http`: optional. `responseCache(db, tables)`, the Postgres `ResponseCache` for `idempotent()` from `@arki/http/idempotency` (HTTP replay on `journal_receipts`; not the command receipt).
- `@arki/journal/foreman`: optional. The Foreman job console `journalJobsModule({ journal, db })` (reads, retry, discard, cancel, purge, replay, with previews and approvals), its `JOURNAL_JOBS_ERROR_CODES` (`ARKI_JOURNAL_E001` to `E005`), and `journalReceiptStore` / `foremanReceiptTables` (moved from `@arki/admin/pg`). Needs the optional peer `@arki/admin`.
- `@arki/journal/http/webhooks`: optional, Node or Bun. Outgoing webhooks on the job table: `webhookTables()`, `webhookSender({ tables, webhooks, encryptionKey })` with `subscribe`, `dispatch(tx, …)`, `replay`, `rotateSecret`, `enable`, `disable` and the queue `runner`.

## Start here
- [Agent guide](docs/agent-guide.md): the model, the three objects, the task map, the rules, the error table. Read it first.

- [Wire it in a Dot app](docs/agent-guide.md#dot), or [ship journal pieces from a shared package](docs/agent-guide.md#shared-packages)

## Files
- Public surface: `src/index.ts` (the exports), `src/api.ts` (every public signature), `src/types.ts` (row, event, handler and database types), `src/errors.ts` (the codes and their messages, the command failures and `CommandError`), `src/hooks.ts` (around-hooks on command and effect runs).
- Definitions: `src/journal.ts` (`initJournal`, `j`, `j.compose`), `src/entity.ts` (entity builder, reducers, key checks), `src/event.ts` (`j.event`), `src/handlers.ts` (`j.projection`, `j.effect`, `need`, and `bindEffect`, which gives an effect its services).
- Write path: `src/command.ts` (`journal.run`), `src/journal.ts` (`journal.bind`),`src/write.ts` (the write steps), `src/fold.ts` (apply events to a row), `src/storage.ts` (load and save the row, id and value checks), `src/transaction-guard.ts` (one operation per transaction).
- After commit and repair: `src/worker.ts` (`drain`, the worker loop, `wake`, `strandedJobs`), `src/history.ts` (`replay`, `verify`, `repair`, `rerun`).
- Job operations and retention: `src/outbox.ts` (`createJobOps`: reads, verbs, sweep steps), `src/retention.ts` (`Keep`, defaults, `ndjsonArchiveSink`), `src/foreman/index.ts` (the Foreman module).
- Edges: `src/pg.ts` (the tables), `src/dot.ts` (Dot plugin), `src/orpc.ts` (oRPC error mapping),`src/id.ts` (id factories, name checks), `src/debug.ts` (`DEBUG=arki:journal:*`), `src/test-support.ts` (test fixture, not shipped).

## Rules that bite
- The door is `journal.bind(db, meta)`: bind once per request or job, then call `run(command, input)`. You give `meta`; the library never picks an actor.
- A rule that rejects a request returns a failure (`CommandNotFound({ detail })` and the others, or the app's own). The command rolls back exactly as for a throw, and `journal.run` returns it, typed. An `events` failure comes back from `write`, a child's from `run`: return it from the handler. A command that got one and still returns a success throws `IGNORED_FAILURE` and commits nothing. To handle a refusal on purpose, check it and call `accept(result)` (on the command and the effect context): it lifts only this command's check, once per return of that very value; the refused child stays rolled back. Misuse throws `INVALID_ACCEPT`. Throwing `CommandError(code, message)` still works. Neither is a `JournalError`. An oRPC app adds `commandErrors()` once, after its own error middleware; it answers a returned failure as an error too.
- Await every `write` and `run`. One journal operation per transaction at a time. No `Promise.all` over writes.
- `drain` and `worker` take the root database, never a transaction.
- An effect that needs a service lists it: `j.effect(name, entity, { mailer: need<Mailer>() }, on)`. The handler reads `mailer` from its context. Do not wrap an effect in a function. A plain app gives the services once, in `j.compose({ services })`. In a Dot app the feature that lists the effect declares them in `needs`.
- Any running worker can claim any job. Run the worker in the process that holds what its effects talk to (for example an in-memory emitter).
- A reducer returns the value the database will store, or the write fails with `VALUE_MISMATCH`. Returning `null` deletes the row. A soft delete is a normal patch.
- Version 1 means created by the journal. A row that existed before the journal starts at version 2.
- Pass ids exactly as they are stored. Events are frozen: copy before you change.

> The design spec (`docs/specs/2026-10-09-journal-design.md`) explains intent. `src/api.ts` defines the signatures. When they differ, `src/api.ts` is right.
